title: The Truth of the Witness
english: Since the poet who said that the Cretans are always liars, wild beasts, and lazy bellies (Titus 1:12), seizing these words, said that they badly demonstrate the tomb of a non-existent Zeus, Paul used the same verse so that it might not be thought that he runs to the poet and that the one called Zeus witnesses immortality; he brought it forward. This witness is true. That one lied by supporting Zeus, but I speak truthfully, saying that the Cretans are always liars and lazy bellies. This witness is true, not that one.
Since he often teaches moderation in praise (Titus 1:13), but he found the Cretans having need of something like a center of striking, because of this he said that they are sharp.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Fragmenta in epistulam ad Titum u01-open

title: Acknowledgment vs Denial in Works
english: They confess to know God, but in works they deny [him].
He showed that he calls women to an inheritance (Tit 2:3); for he would not have said [they are] fit for priestly service (Tit 2:3).

title: Intellect and Dignity in Work
english: He took hold of it through the intellect, but that which pertains to dignity is in the work, so that he might abstain not only from corruptible work but also from corruptible thought.
